newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil premiums stable, screen curbs volume.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil premiums stable, screen curbs volume.

text.p: European gas oil outright prices firmed and premiums were stable to slightly stronger in thin physical business on Wednesday, traders said.
The front month August IPE contract firmed $1.50 a tonne to $169.25. September was up $1.25 at $170.25.
Physical demand was curbed by stronger futures, lack of arbitrage and the continuing robust performance of the dollar against the mark.
"German buyers will wait for easier numbers. A big price dip will be bought," a trader said.
The U.S. currency was trading at 1.8442 marks at 1200 GMT, just off a 7-1/2 year high recorded on Monday.

A European major was heard willing to buy a 10,000 cargo of German heating oil for around August IPE +$1/$1.50. The stem was offered at $2 premium. Russian heating oil was bid slightly firmer at a 25 to 50 cent premium to August. Diesel cargoes were discussed steady at August Ipe +$3.50/$4.50.

On the ARA barge market, prompt Rotterdam refinery was done at August IPE +$1 and +$0.50, with the latter seen nearer the talked market. A small prompt diesel barge was done at a $4 premium to August IPE, an unchanged level.
